findings.issue: Heteronym: the meaning includes 铅 (metal, /lɛd/), but only /liːd/ is shown; the example uses the noun lead /liːd/.
findings.context: The team followed her lead during the crisis.

findings.issue: Ambiguous heteronym: adjective live is /laɪv/, verb live is /lɪv/; both are listed, but the example forces the adjective reading.
findings.context: We watched a live broadcast from the stadium.

findings.issue: Stress heteronym: noun is /ˈɪnkriːs/, verb is /ɪnˈkriːs/; meaning and example are the noun.
findings.context: There has been an increase in sales this year.

findings.issue: IPA gives the letter names “I T” (/aɪ ti/), not the pronoun /ɪt/.
findings.context: It was raining when we arrived.

findings.issue: IPA is empty for the pronoun I /aɪ/.
IPA is empty; the example uses lies /laɪz/, while the base form lie is /laɪ/.
findings.context: The old books lie on the top shelf.
I lost the key to my front door.
She found a new job at a small software company.
He wore a clean pair of jeans to the interview.
The morning sun stayed low behind the hills.
There was a small mark on the white wall.

findings.issue: IPA contains an invisible zero-width space between ɝ and ɡ.
findings.context: He ordered a hamburger and a glass of water.

result.notes: No audio was supplied, so findings concern text/IPA only. Ordinary American/British variants and approved alternatives were not flagged. The source uses a broad simplified transcription in many entries (e.g., e for /eɪ/, o for /oʊ/, omitted length marks); those systemic conventions were not flagged individually. Blank IPA entries were treated as data gaps rather than pronunciation variants.
